Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that its former employees "stole trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI."

It is reported that, as part of the litigation process, Apple has directly sent letters to dozens of former employees who currently work at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued litigation hold notices to approximately 40 former employees.

A litigation hold notice is a formal written notice sent to individuals or organizations, requiring them to preserve documents, records and other evidence that may be relevant to legal disputes. Such letters usually specify the exact materials that should be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the theft of trade secrets may involve more parties than just those named as defendants in last week's initial lawsuit.

For reference, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan, as defendants.
